description: One-time-use enforcement ledger for per-client-limited promotion codes (starting with the '2X1' welcome coupon granted on a client's first purchase). A filtered UNIQUE index on (companyId, clientId, promotionCode) makes a second redemption of the same code by the same client impossible at the database level. This closes a real gap: the POS Cart UI only offers the coupon when the client's posRewardBalances.lifetimeEarned is zero (a client-side heuristic), but nothing stops a direct call to /income/apply-promo from reusing the code for a client who already spent it. Distinct from posRewardTransactions/posRewardRedemptions (points-based loyalty currency, spent against a rewards catalog) — this ledger tracks one-time promo-code usage, not points, and never converts between the two.

fields.name: clientId
fields.description: Client who redeemed the promotion code.

fields.name: promotionCode
fields.description: Code redeemed, stored uppercase (e.g. '2X1'). Matches income.promotionCode and the code param already sent to sp_income_apply_promo. This module does not define or validate which codes exist/are active — an existing promotions table already does that server-side (outside this repo/PRD); this module only guards how many times each client may use a given code.

fields.name: incomeId
fields.description: Ticket the code's discount was applied to. Always set on a normal redemption; only NULL for a redemption attempted and immediately reversed before an income row existed.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Allowed values: applied, reversed. A reversed row (from voiding/cancelling the paired income) does not count against the one-time limit — the client can redeem the code again.

fields.name: redeemedByUserId
fields.description: POS user/cashier who processed the sale that redeemed the code.

relationships.notes: Multi-tenant isolation via companyId — injected automatically by stored procedures.
clientId owns the redemption; the one-time limit is scoped per (companyId, clientId, promotionCode).

components.name: PromotionRedemptionListStep
components.description: IonList of redemptions newest-first, filtered by companyId + optional clientId/promotionCode. Rows show client name, promotionCode chip, incomeId (linkable to the ticket), status badge (applied green / reversed grey), redeemedByUserId, created_At. Read-only audit view — Admin/Manager only; cashiers never browse this list, they only trigger a redemption implicitly through checkout.

endpoints.description: Read-only pre-check the Cart UI calls before offering the coupon chip. Takes { companyId, clientId, promotionCode }. Returns { eligible: boolean } — eligible=true only if no row with status='applied' exists yet for (companyId, clientId, promotionCode). Decides eligibility only, never a discount amount or price — that stays entirely in sp_income_apply_promo.

The only path allowed to insert a row. Takes { companyId, clientId, promotionCode, incomeId, redeemedByUserId }. Transactionally: (1) checks for an existing status='applied' row for (companyId, clientId, promotionCode) — if found, rolls back and returns { error: 'already_redeemed' }, never a partial write; (2) otherwise inserts this row with status='applied'. This must be called from inside the same transaction as sp_income_apply_promo (see database hints below) so the one-time limit is enforced atomically in the database, not just by call ordering from the client — two concurrent checkout requests for the same client+code must not both succeed.

Takes { companyId, redemptionId, reversedByUserId }. Sets status='reversed'. Called from the existing income-cancel path (POST /income action=2) when the paired ticket is voided, so cancelling a sale returns the one-time coupon to the client. Never physically deletes the row — same audit-trail requirement as posRewardRedemptions.

hints: Filtered UNIQUE index on (companyId, clientId, promotionCode) WHERE status='applied' — this is the actual one-time-use guarantee; a reversed row must not block a later redemption of the same code by the same client.

sp_promotionRedemptions_redeem must be transactional exactly like sp_posRewardRedemptions_redeem: check-then-insert inside one transaction, never two separate round trips, so a race between two concurrent checkout requests for the same client+code cannot both succeed.

MANUAL INTEGRATION REQUIRED, outside this PRD's auto-generated scope: sp_income_apply_promo (the existing SP behind POST /income/apply-promo, defined in the income module, not this one) must be edited to call sp_promotionRedemptions_redeem inside its own transaction before discounting income.total, and must roll back the whole promo application if that call returns already_redeemed. Until sp_income_apply_promo is edited to do this, this module only provides an advisory /check-eligibility the frontend can call — it does not by itself close the gap, because nothing stops a caller from skipping straight to /income/apply-promo.
Similarly, wiring sp_promotionRedemptions_reverse into the income-cancel path (existing action=2 handling in the income module) needs a manual pass in that module, not this one.
Index (clientId, promotionCode) for the eligibility check; index (companyId, created_At DESC) for the admin audit list.
